newsitem.title: UK: N.Irish police hold two after church arson.
newsitem.headline: N.Irish police hold two after church arson.

text.p: Northern Ireland police said on Sunday they were holding two men suspected of trying to burn down a Roman Catholic church at Carrickfergus town north of Belfast.
The early Saturday morning blaze was the fifth at a Catholic church in the past month and the latest in a series of church burnings believed started by rival sectarian gangs in the British province.

In another violent incident in the troubled region, a 13-year-old boy was reported to have been admitted to hospital with an eye injury after a clash late between rioters and British troops in the town of Lurgan south of Belfast late Saturday.
Security sources said that troops fired a plastic bullet when a crowd attacked them with stones and other missiles.
Tension has been high in the province since Irish Republican Army fighters, who are supported by some minority Catholics, resumed a guerrilla campaign against British rule.
Protestant extremists loyal to London have launched several retaliatory attacks on random Catholics.
Over 16 months 56 Protestant and Catholic churches and 45 community halls used by the different denominations have been damaged by arsonists.
Police sources said a man of 18 and another aged 19 would be kept in custody until a court appearance on Monday on charges of arson at the church of St Nicholas in Carrickfergus.
The roof and interior were badly damaged. Catholic and Protestant church leaders visited the church and described the attack as obscene.
The arsonists got in by removing wire-mesh security grills on a window. "They tried to set the church on fire in seven different points inside," said a parishioner David Kane.
